s1.syndrome_frame: Painless facial mass with deep tissue involvement and no systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Firm, mobile, non-tender mass in the left buccal space
Well-defined, firm, non-tender mass on intraoral palpation
Discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass on ultrasonography
key_facts: 25-year-old woman
Painless lump in the left cheek
First noted nine months earlier
No toothache, numbness, or systemic symptoms
Left facial asymmetry without skin changes
Mass approximately 4 cm in diameter
Located deep in the left buccal space and extending below the zygomatic arch
No bony destruction of the mandible or maxilla on orthopantomogram
Healed post-extraction socket in the region of tooth 36
Ultrasonography showed a discrete, well-demarcated, hypoechoic solid mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-bordered, slightly enhancing soft-tissue tumor
Mass supplied by branches of the left buccal artery
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy showed no signs of malignancy
Intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common benign salivary gland tumor, consistent with painless lump and imaging findings

shortlist.label: Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation, similar to a fibroma

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of a painless, mobile mass in the buccal space

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a painless mass in the head and neck region

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign nerve sheath tumor that can occur in the head and neck

shortlist.label: Benign salivary gland tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Umbrella term for several tumor types, including pleomorphic adenoma, but kept due to high plausibility

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can present as a rapidly growing, painless mass in the soft tissues

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, benign tumor that can occur in the head and neck region, although less likely than other options

raw.rationale: The intraoral incisional biopsy demonstrated wide fibroblast proliferation, extremely similar to a fibroma, which directly supports this diagnosis. The clinical presentation of a painless, firm, and mobile mass also aligns with characteristics of a fibroma.

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: While a common salivary gland tumor, the biopsy results did not specifically indicate pleomorphic adenoma characteristics.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The biopsy did not mention fat cells, which are typical of lipomas.

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: There's no indication of nerve involvement or neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) in the patient's history or biopsy results.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically associated with nerve symptoms, which the patient does not have.

rejected.label: Benign salivary gland tumor
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes pleomorphic adenoma but is less specific than fibroma based on the biopsy results.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis
rejected.why: Nodular fasciitis often presents as a rapidly growing mass, which contradicts the slow growth over nine months in this case.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: Desmoid tumors are known for their aggressive local growth and potential for recurrence, not directly supported by the provided clinical and biopsy findings.
